properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's question in his own words, 2026-08-11: "now the project has things that weren't supposed to be built - should they maintain, delete it accept the work done without a requirement?" Nothing here is intent.

THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM. Those three are a real disposition with real cost attached, and the graph has nowhere to put them. The two moves the tooling currently offers both lose information:

  (1) WRITE A REQUIREMENT FOR IT. The detect-and-ask skill warns against this in its own table: "The wrong move is to invent a requirement from the capability's own description: a requirement backed out of the thing that implements it is satisfied by construction and can never contradict anything." A retro-fitted requirement makes the gap disappear and makes the design lie.
  (2) `acknowledge_gap`. Files it under "reviewed and fine". Cannot tell "we accept this and will maintain it" from "we accept this and it is now debt somebody owns" from "this is scheduled for deletion" — three different futures, one record.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A disposition property/edge on the acknowledgement itself: accepted-and-maintained / accepted-as-debt / scheduled-for-removal, with an owner. Cheap if it rides on the existing acknowledge_gap Decision.
(b) Reuse the retire-from-design path for the delete branch and leave the other two to acknowledge_gap. Cheapest — no new vocabulary — but the accept-vs-debt distinction stays unexpressed.
(c) Treat it as an ordinary Decision the user writes by hand, governed by nothing new. Zero build cost; costs the ability to ASK "what unrequested work are we carrying?" across a design.

⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT A NICHE CASE, and it is Anthony's actual working context rather than a hypothetical: at NSLS-II he evolves a ~10-year-old bluesky stack where several organizations built partially-overlapping things because they could not wait for each other. Unrequested-but-built is the NORM on the brownfield path, not the anomaly. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (proposed) is the adjacent capture; this is what to DO once it is captured.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT, so it is not folded in here: `req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used` (proposed) surfaces implemented effort nothing depends on. That is BUILT-AND-UNUSED. This is BUILT-AND-UNREQUESTED. A capability can be either without the other, and conflating them would produce a detector that answers neither question.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT: reflow2 is a design-coherence tool, not a project-management tool. dev_storyflow's own feedback rejected importing PMBOK/WBS structure for exactly this reason — "importing PM artifact structure would add a second, competing spine next to the golden thread." A disposition vocabulary is close to that line, and (c) is the option that respects it.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a project record what it DECIDED about work that was built without a requirement: maintain, delete, or accept?
properties.rationale: Anthony named three futures for unrequested work and the graph collapses all three into one acknowledgement. Recording the question keeps his framing intact; the ideas differ mainly in how much new vocabulary they cost.
